english: Mother, sleep does not come to me. Sing me a song. What do you want? The song of the bird. My grandmother sang it. Daughter, lie down and listen to it. The bird sang to its young by the fire (?). Your voice is sweet. Now sleep comes. May sweet sleep/dream come to you.
uncertain: h₂éwey moy péh₂ura h₂éwey téḱnōy séngʷʰe: unclear, péh₂ura looks like a plural of 'fire'

english: Old shepherd, why do you call on the gods early? Father Sky, Mother Earth and Fire. Why do you call Fire? Fire carries the words to the other immortals. It goes to the divine mouth. Does Fire hear a word I speak otherwise? It does not hear. Speak the words straight. Now show me the words, old shepherd.
uncertain: h₁yód h₂élyod h₁nómn̥ wérh₁oh₂: 'a word that I say differently'?

english: What are you making at night by the fire? I am fashioning words. A woman weaves wool; I fashion a hymn. Whom does it praise? It praises the king's son, who went beyond the border. Does the king give you gold? He gives what the hymn is worth. Now I will fashion it.
uncertain: h₁yód h₁erkʷós h₁wésus: 'what is good for the hymn'

english: Host, I praise your name with a gift-song. What will you give me? I will give you a cow, and she gives much milk. She is good. My hymn is worth two cows. You are bold, friend. Now proclaim two cows, bronze, and fame for me at the feast. I will proclaim it, and your fame will be imperishable.
uncertain: ḱn̥sdʰí 2sg imperative 'proclaim' addressed to the singer: odd

english: Brother, why are you angry? I sang for the chief for three nights, and he gave me a small cup. A small cup. What will you do? I will make a new song at the feast. The chief's heart is small, and he gives nothing from his hand. The people laugh. Won't he be angry? Let him be angry. A bad name lives long.
uncertain: first sentence has no verb of singing, only 'song' accusative

english: Who taught you, old man? You know many songs. My grandfather taught me first. His name was famous. What did he teach first? To sit at his feet at night and to listen. Shall I still sit at your feet? Sit soon, and give me your ears.
